The '''Minkowski sausage'''<ref>{{cite book|last=Lauwerier |first=Hans |title=Fractals: Endlessly Repeated Geometrical Figures |url=https://archive.org/details/fractalsendlessl00lauw |url-access=registration |publisher=Princeton University Press |date=1991 |isbn=0-691-02445-6 |page=[https://archive.org/details/fractalsendlessl00lauw/page/37 37] |quote=The so-called Minkowski sausage. Mandelbrot gave it this name to honor the friend and colleague of Einstein who died so untimely (1864-1909). |translator-last1=Gill-Hoffstädt |translator-first1=Sophia }}<!--Original 1987 in Dutch.--></ref> or '''Minkowski curve''' is a [[fractal]] first proposed by and named for [[Hermann Minkowski]] as well as its casual resemblance to a [[sausage]] or sausage links. The initiator is a [[line segment]] and the generator is a [[polygonal chain|broken line]] of eight parts one fourth the length.<ref name="Addison">Addison, Paul (1997). ''Fractals and Chaos: An illustrated course'', p. 19. CRC Press. {{ISBN|0849384435}}.</ref>

The Sausage has a [[Hausdorff dimension]] of <math>\left ( \ln8/\ln4\ \right ) = 1.5 = 3/2</math>.{{efn|name=Type 2}} It is therefore often chosen when studying the physical properties of non-integer fractal objects. It is strictly [[self-similar]].<ref name="Addison"/> It never intersects itself. It is [[continuous function|continuous]] everywhere, but [[differentiable function|differentiable]] nowhere. It is not [[rectifiable curve|rectifiable]]. It has a [[Lebesgue measure]] of 0. The type 1 curve has a dimension of {{sfrac|ln 5|ln 3}}&nbsp;≈&nbsp;1.46.{{efn|name=Type 1}}

Multiple Minkowski Sausages may be arranged in a four sided polygon or [[square]] to create a quadratic [[Koch island]] or '''Minkowski island/[snow]flake''':
